title: Cauliflower and Cheese Soup
subtitle: Smooth cauliflower soup finished with sharp cheddar
excerpt: Cauliflower blended with a light vegetable stock base into a velvety soup, then finished with a generous amount of strong Cheddar. Creamy without relying on cream, and ready in under 40 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cauliflower is one of the most naturally sweet and starchy brassicas, which makes it ideal for smooth soups that feel rich without heavy cream. The Cheddar melts easily into the hot blended soup, adding sharpness and body. Using a mature Cheddar gives the best flavour. The soup thickens as it stands: thin it with a splash of hot water or stock before serving if it has tightened up.

recipeTools.notes: For blending directly in the pot.

content.text: The cheese goes in off the heat: returning the soup to a hard boil after adding Cheddar can make it grainy. Blend the soup as smooth as possible before adding the cheese for the best texture. A small amount of mustard sharpens the flavour without announcing itself.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cauliflower florets and stalk. Pour in the hot stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until the cauliflower is completely tender.
Remove from the heat. Blend until very smooth. Stir in the mustard and most of the Cheddar. Stir until the cheese has melted. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into warmed bowls. Top with the remaining grated Cheddar. Serve with crusty bread.
